drafts.neutral_framing: Travis County already publishes every payment online. Should it take the next step no Texas government has — publishing item-level purchase-card spending, the way Oklahoma does?
drafts.final_wording: Should Travis County publish item-level purchase-card spending — what was bought, not only who was paid?
drafts.final_wording_note: Framed around the next level of detail beyond the check-level disclosure Travis County already provides.
shaping_notes: A policy question about disclosure format, not any person — clears the bright lines.
Grounded in fact: Travis runs a Vendor Payment Register that ties payments to invoices/POs; no Texas local government publishes item-level purchase-card data, and Oklahoma is the lone benchmark.
drafts.tier_note: Open as a Tier 0 sentiment poll: no account, one voice per browser, changeable until close. Tier 0 is displayed but never cited as verified resident opinion.
drafts.background: Travis County’s Vendor Payment Register lets anyone search payments and see the invoices and purchase orders behind them. Item-level purchase-card data — what was bought, not just who was paid — is the next level of detail. Oklahoma posts every state purchase-card transaction, itemized (Oklahoma open data); we found no Texas local government that does.
